bridges.description: Show that historical Bibles sometimes attribute non-original wording to Jesus.
Show that a recoverable ancestor need not reproduce the autograph.
Show that some viable variants materially affect interpretation.
Explain why uncertainty challenged Ehrman’s former inspiration view.
Show that variants are not misquotations because wording and message remain recoverable.
Show that distributed transmission preserves readings without central control.
Distinguish raw totals from meaningful viable variants and message continuity.
Show that perfect copies or unanimous certainty are not required.

moves.inference: Some historical Bibles contain Jesus material that may not be original.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Events 445–765 preserve the essential qualification before the cumulative examples; the longer span is necessary to prevent the examples from being mistaken for a claim that every variant is significant.

omittedMaterial.reason: Biographical framing, greetings, humor, and timekeeping are peripheral rather than substitutes for an argument.
Additional manuscript images and devotional framing repeat the already selected distributed-preservation and message-continuity inferences.
Authority lists and repeated credential challenges were reviewed; every distinct evidential test and later qualification is represented by a selected move.
Audience Q&A and outro are excluded and supply no credit, penalty, concession, or missing-reply inference.

speakerAttributionReview.method: Named handoffs, formal rounds, addressees, and first-person continuity; canonical zero-based events define spans.
handoffs: Shared boundary events 1539, 1892, and 3505 were handled without assigning carryover to the next speaker.
speakerAttributionReview.mixedSpans: Questions are context only; claims and quotes belong solely to the named respondent.
speakerAttributionReview.audioVerification: No direct human listening or diarization occurred; five automated checks are limited aids.
speakerAttributionReview.remainingUncertainty: No selected claim depends on corrupted Greek, names, dates, or the four-tenths error; attribution is high.

selectionBalanceAudit.rationale: The asymmetry follows the source: White separately tests early dating, denominators, tenacity, Hebrews, Mark, classical consistency, apostolic practice, convergence, education, and the final motion, while Ehrman’s fewer moves preserve his distinct qualifications and countermodels.

sections.rationale: The fourth row covers a source-distinct, nonmergeable reciprocal test identified in the coverage audit; merging it would erase its separate premise or qualification.
